//: The sources this plugin ships with, so nobody has to configure one to get started. Written from docs/05-sources.md, which is the specification; every address here was measured answering a real release name end to end on 13 August 2026.
//hosts: Every host below is also in plugin.json under capabilities.network.hosts, including the ones belonging to a disabled source: the manifest cannot change at runtime, so a source the owner switches on later needs its host permitted already. A test holds the two lists together in both directions.

sources.name: PreDB
sources.note: A name database with an RSS search. Gating is a property of an address: the feed answers over plain HTTP and the search sits behind a challenge. It answers a plain curl with an empty feed but answers the plugin, so do not conclude it is dead from a shell test.

sources.name: srrDB
sources.note: Names only. Served as text/html and is XML regardless.

sources.name: srrDB search
sources.note: JSON with resultsCount and results[].release. Names, not torrents, and that is the point: only a full release name is fit to put to an indexer. A show with no scene releases honestly answers zero, which is not a broken reader.

sources.name: SceneSource
sources.note: Read through the browser. It is a feed and has no search: 0.3.4 put it in the search set and made forty identical requests per cycle.

sources.name: EZTV latest
sources.note: JSON, and must not be read as HTML. It takes a search parameter and ignores it, so it is read whole on the feed pass and never asked a question.

sources.name: The Pirate Bay
sources.note: JSON, with an info hash and honest seeder counts per row. The website itself is a JavaScript shell with no results in it; this is what it calls. Rate-limits hard under a burst.

sources.name: 1337x
sources.note: The category-scoped address only: a plain search with dots returns their error page, which says 'No results were returned' and is not an error. No magnet on the listing; the row carries its own page address.

sources.name: LimeTorrents
sources.note: A hashed .torrent link on the listing, which the generic reader handles.

sources.name: TorrentBay
sources.note: Publishes no magnet: it comes from a signed POST to its own endpoint, built from two values off the row and two off the search page, sent from inside the browser session.

sources.name: EZTV
sources.note: Appends [eztv.re] to every title; strip it or nothing matches.

sources.name: KickassTorrents
sources.note: Four anchors per row and three empty; the name is in cellMainLink, cut into highlighted fragments that must be joined. A search for a full release name often redirects to that release's own page.

sources.name: TorrentGalaxy
sources.note: Searches from its path, where a plus is a plus. No magnet and no hash on the listing: the forty-character hex strings there are element ids.

sources.name: Torrentz2
sources.note: Twenty definition lists, each with a name and a link to its own page. Titles carry a site prefix to cut, anchored on ' - ' with spaces because a scene name is full of dashes and the one before the group has none.

sources.name: TorrentDownloads
sources.note: The first link is an advert for another site carrying the same terms, so rows are matched on the numeric id every real release has in its address.

sources.name: TorrentFunk
sources.note: A query with spaces gets a 301 to nothing. Attributes are bare: class=tv3, not class="tv3". The detail page carries no magnet but prints the bare info hash.

sources.name: Nyaa
sources.note: An indexer in XML; every item links a real torrent. For anime it is often the only source that has the release, and it is asked with both the seasonal and the absolute form.

sources.name: YTS
sources.note: Films, which are out of scope for this plugin. Shipped switched off so the address is recorded and never asked.
